ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, extend the hypotenuse $BC$ to point $D$ so that $CD = \frac{1}{2}BC$. Connect $AD$. If $\tan B = \frac{4}{3}$, what is the value of $\tan \angle CAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line $CF \perp AC$ intersecting $AD$ at point $F$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACF=90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, \\
it implies $AB\parallel CF$, \\
hence $\angle DCF=\angle DBA$, \\
thus $\triangle DCF\sim \triangle DBA$, \\
implying $\frac{CF}{AB}=\frac{CD}{BD}$, \\
since $CD=\frac{1}{2}BC$, \\
thus $CD=\frac{1}{3}BD$, \\
that is $\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{1}{3}$, \\
thus $\frac{CF}{AB}=\frac{1}{3}$, \\
hence $CF=\frac{1}{3}AB$, \\
In right $\triangle ABC$, \\
since $\tan B=\frac{4}{3}$, that is $\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{4}{3}$, \\
let $AC=4x$, then $AB=3x$, \\
thus $CF=\frac{1}{3} \times 3x=x$, \\
therefore $\tan\angle CAD=\frac{CF}{AC}=\frac{x}{4x}=\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$.

图像描述：附图中，A 点在上方，B、C、D 三点在下方同一直线上，C 位于 B 与 D 之间，D 是从 C 继续向右延长得到的点；线段 AB、AC 构成三角形 ABC，A 处标有直角符号，表示 ∠BAC = 90°；线段 AD 已连接，要求的是 AC 与 AD 之间的角 ∠CAD 的正切值。
推理：按坐标/向量方法处理。因为 ∠A = 90°，且 tan B = AC/AB = 4/3，可不失一般性地取 A = (0,0)，令 AB 在 x 轴正方向上，B = (3,0)，令 AC 在 y 轴正方向上，C = (0,4)。此时 BC = 5。D 在 BC 经过 C 的延长线上，且 CD = 1/2 BC，所以向量 CD = 1/2 向量 BC = 1/2(C - B)。因此 D = C + 1/2(C - B) = (0,4) + 1/2((-3,4)) = (-3/2,6)。于是向量 AD = (-3/2,6)。∠CAD 是从 AC 方向，即竖直方向，到 AD 的夹角，其正切等于水平偏移量除以竖直偏移量，所以 tan ∠CAD = (3/2)/6 = 1/4。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This method avoids auxiliary similarity triangles and instead encodes the whole diagram in coordinates, using vector extension along BC to locate D directly.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the incidence/order information: A is the right-angle vertex, AB and AC are perpendicular legs, B-C-D are collinear in that order, and AD is connected.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use CD = 1/2 BC to locate D on the ray from B through C, and tan B = 4/3 to choose the 3-4-5 right-triangle scale.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use coordinate placement under rigid motion/scaling, the right-triangle tangent ratio, the vector formula for extending a segment, and slope/tangent interpretation relative to the chosen axis.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, extend the hypotenuse $BC$ to point $D$ so that $CD = \frac{1}{2}BC$. Connect $AD$. If $\tan B = \frac{4}{3}$, what is the value of $\tan \angle CAD$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line $CF \perp AC$ intersecting $AD$ at point $F$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACF=90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, \\
it implies $AB\parallel CF$, \\
hence $\angle DCF=\angle DBA$, \\
thus $\triangle DCF\sim \triangle DBA$, \\
implying $\frac{CF}{AB}=\frac{CD}{BD}$, \\
since $CD=\frac{1}{2}BC$, \\
thus $CD=\frac{1}{3}BD$, \\
that is $\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{1}{3}$, \\
thus $\frac{CF}{AB}=\frac{1}{3}$, \\
hence $CF=\frac{1}{3}AB$, \\
In right $\triangle ABC$, \\
since $\tan B=\frac{4}{3}$, that is $\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{4}{3}$, \\
let $AC=4x$, then $AB=3x$, \\
thus $CF=\frac{1}{3} \times 3x=x$, \\
therefore $\tan\angle CAD=\frac{CF}{AC}=\frac{x}{4x}=\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a geometric figure; points B, C, D are on the same horizontal straight line, with C located between B and D; point A is above, and AB, AC, AD are connected. There is a right-angle mark at A, indicating ∠BAC = 90°, so ABC is a right triangle with A as the right angle, BC is the hypotenuse, and BC is extended to D. Reasoning: According to the method, draw an auxiliary line; through C draw CF ⟂ AC, intersecting AD at F. Because in the figure ∠BAC = 90°, that is, AB ⟂ AC, and CF ⟂ AC, so CF ∥ AB. Also because B, C, D are collinear, and A, F, D are collinear, ∠DCF = ∠DBA, and ∠CDF = ∠BDA, therefore △DCF ∼ △DBA. From similar triangles, CF/AB = CD/BD. It is known that CD = 1/2 BC, and BD = BC + CD = BC + 1/2 BC = 3/2 BC, so CD/BD = (1/2 BC)/(3/2 BC) = 1/3. Therefore CF/AB = 1/3, that is, CF = AB/3. In right triangle ABC, tan B = AC/AB = 4/3; let AB = 3x, AC = 4x, then CF = AB/3 = x. Because F is on AD, and CF ⟂ AC, so ∠CAF = ∠CAD; in right triangle ACF, tan ∠CAD = CF/AC = x/(4x) = 1/4.
